title: Retro Bedroom Portfolio
subtitle: This Very Site
shortDescription: The site you are on — an interactive portfolio styled as a 2000s bedroom PC, built content-first with Astro.
longDescription: This portfolio is itself a project: an interactive room scene inspired by 2000–2005 bedroom PCs, point-and-click games, CRT displays, and pixel icons. The rule is portfolio first, game-like second — every piece of content is semantic HTML reachable by direct URL, and the adventure layer never gates access. It is built with Astro content collections, a documented design system, and a phase-by-phase spec-driven process.
problem: Developer portfolios blur together — the challenge was being memorable and expressive without sacrificing accessibility, performance, or direct access to content.
solution: A content-first architecture: projects, experience, and skills are structured content rendered as semantic HTML on direct routes, with the retro bedroom scene layered on top as enhancement rather than a gate.
responsibilities: Wrote the full spec — PRD, design system, interaction and motion specs, accessibility, performance budgets
Built the Astro site — content collections, layouts, and a hand-rolled retro UI component kit
Designed and produced the pixel-art asset pack and original WAV cues
Held the accessibility line — keyboard access, reduced motion, audio off by default
features: Interactive bedroom scene with hotspots and a quest log
File-explorer project browser with per-project case studies
Direct-route URLs for all content — no puzzle required
Original pixel-art assets and WAV UI cues

decisions.title: Portfolio first, game-like second
decisions.rationale: A visitor must reach every project and the contact page without solving a puzzle — the room is enhancement, not a gate.

decisions.title: Content collections as source of truth
decisions.rationale: Projects are typed JSON documents rendered through a schema, so case studies stay consistent.

decisions.title: No heavy framework
decisions.rationale: Static Astro output keeps the site fast; the retro UI is hand-rolled instead of pulled from a component library.

impact: Doubles as a living demo of spec-driven design and front-end craft
